📝 Docs-Driven AI (Part 1): Stop Writing Scattered Prompts, Start Controlling AI with YAML & Markdown!
Ever felt frustrated when you ask AI (like ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, or Gemini) to help write code for your system, but after a few prompts, the AI starts going off the rails? 😅
At first, the code looks great. But by the 5th or 6th prompt, the AI suddenly forgets the tech stack you’re using. You ask for TailwindCSS, and it gives you inline CSS. You tell it to use PostgreSQL, and it creates a schema for MongoDB.
The end result? You waste more time fixing the AI’s mistakes than writing the code yourself. Exhausting, right? And you’re paying for it too… 💸💸💸
That’s where the “Docs-Driven AI Development” concept comes in.
Think of the AI like a Junior Developer who types super fast but forgets easily. You can’t just give verbal instructions (or simple prompts) and expect it to remember everything. You need an official Blueprint. And the best blueprint for AI today is a combination of YAML Frontmatter and Markdown.
Let’s dive into this concept! 🚀
💡 What Is the YAML + Markdown Concept?
In short, we’ll create a text file (usually named prd.md, blueprint.md, or spec.md). This file will be divided into two main sections:
1. ⚙️ YAML Frontmatter (Fixed Rules / Hard Rules)
Ever seen a Markdown file that starts with --- at the top and bottom? That’s Frontmatter.
This is where we put metadata and ironclad rules that the AI absolutely cannot break, no matter what. AI is great at reading YAML format (key-value structure). This is where we “lock” the AI’s brain:
•
Role: “Act as a Senior Full-Stack Developer.”
•
Tech Stack: Next.js, TailwindCSS, Prisma. (When we list them here, the AI won’t dare use any other frameworks).
•
Database Structure: Exact list of tables and columns.
2. 📖 Markdown Body (Logic & Flow / Soft Rules)
Below the YAML block, we’ll use standard Markdown format (headings, bullet points, bold) to describe our system.
•
Features: What can this system do?
•
Business Logic: For example, “If the user’s age is under 18, the ‘Buy’ button must be disabled.”
•
Step-by-Step: Instructions for the AI on which components to build first.
🎯 Why You Must Use This Method?
If you get into the habit of writing this spec file before starting coding, you’ll experience some magic:
•
🛡️ Goodbye AI ‘Hallucinations’: The AI won’t arbitrarily invent non-existent variable names or database tables, because everything is locked in the YAML section.
•
📂 Can Be Stored in Git (Version Control): This blueprint.md file can be committed to GitHub. If there are changes to the system next month, you just update this file and feed it back to the AI. It acts as living documentation.
•
⚡ Lightning-Fast Context: You open a new chat, no need to type long prompts. Just upload this file and say, “Read this file and wait for my instructions.” Boom! The AI instantly understands your entire project.
⏳ Ready for the Practical Part?
By now, you understand why we need this approach. It’s not just about writing code; it’s about managing projects more smartly.
But what does this file actually look like? How do you write YAML that’s easy for AI to understand?
In Part 2, we’ll roll up our sleeves. I’ll share the actual structure of the .md file along with a basic example (Simple Task Management System), and how to feed this file to the AI so it generates perfect code without errors.
Stay tuned and make sure to follow for Part 2! 🔥
